perception_loop.assessment: No successful framed look was obtained anywhere in a large, dense 3800×2200 diagram. The only three look attempts were refused, and the agent finalized without a valid QA render. Consequently there was no credited edit → framed render → adjustment loop and no render-adjust-render sequence. Although standing board renders are normally supplied with state blocks, the transcript shows no evidence that a visible-render observation drove an adjustment; the recorded adjustments were responses to lint text.

lint_etiquette.assessment: Lint was generally treated constructively: initial crowding, containment, covered-content, unreadable-label, crossing, and clipped-text findings were addressed through moves, resizing, route changes, label removal, and one connection deletion. The same lint was not re-fired for more than three consecutive turns without a strategy change, so there was no lint fight. The final recorded pre-QA patch result at turn 10 resolved the remaining clipped-text warning, and the turn-7 deletion resolved the crossing warning. No warning was knowingly committed as an override, so neither a verbatim reason nor a silent override applies.

commit_honesty.assessment: One commit was made. Its summary is broad but is substantially supported by the stage diff: the board contains version classification and version rules, three publication stores with a consistency gate, hybrid vector/keyword retrieval, a permissions step, grounded/cited answer behavior, quarantine/DLQ/repair elements, feedback and coverage-gap elements, and a separate embedding-generation rebuild and rollback lane. The summary does not claim that lint was clean or that visual QA succeeded. No demonstrably seen visual defect was named in the agent's thinking and then concealed in the summary. The deleted embedding-to-retry edge weakens explicit failure-flow connectivity, but the summary's general phrase "failure handling" remains supported by the retained resilience section and nodes, so it is not counted as a false fix claim.

economy.assessment: The session completed in about 4.84 minutes, well inside the 15-minute budget, and finalized without exhausting the 300-turn limit. The 81 recorded patch operations are proportionate to a large systems diagram. There was one meaningful add-then-delete cycle: e-embed-retry was added at turn 4 and deleted at turn 7 to remove connector crossings. The reset_route NO-OP at turn 5 was not repeated, so it is not NO-OP thrash. The three malformed look attempts were wasteful but are principally captured under failed calls and perception.
